subject: Biology
title: RNA: DNA's Messenger
description: Learn RNA: DNA's Messenger in one minute.

hook.text: DNA never leaves the nucleus. It needs a messenger to carry instructions out. Enter RNA.

buildup.text: RNA is single-stranded and uses uracil instead of thymine. It's DNA's working copy.

discovery.text: Messenger RNA carries gene instructions to ribosomes, where proteins are assembled.

twist.text: Some RNA molecules don't carry messages—they fold into enzymes and do chemistry themselves.

climax.text: COVID vaccines use mRNA to teach cells how to recognize the virus—no DNA editing needed.

punchline.text: RNA delivers the message. Proteins do the job.

quiz.question: What role does messenger RNA play?

details.summary: RNA serves as the intermediary between DNA's stored instructions and the protein-building machinery. Messenger RNA carries gene copies from the nucleus to ribosomes, while transfer RNA and ribosomal RNA assist in translating the code into functional proteins.
details.whyItMatters: RNA is not just a passive messenger. It includes catalytic ribozymes, regulatory microRNAs, and the basis of mRNA vaccines. The RNA world hypothesis even suggests RNA was the original molecule of life before DNA evolved.
takeaways: mRNA carries genetic instructions from DNA to ribosomes for translation
tRNA delivers amino acids matching each mRNA codon during translation
Non-coding RNAs regulate gene expression in complex ways

faq.question: What is the difference between DNA and RNA?
faq.answer: RNA is usually single-stranded, uses ribose sugar instead of deoxyribose, and contains uracil instead of thymine. These differences make RNA less stable but more versatile, able to fold into functional shapes and catalyze chemical reactions.

faq.question: How did mRNA become the basis for COVID vaccines?
faq.answer: mRNA vaccines deliver synthetic mRNA encoding the spike protein into cells. Ribosomes translate this mRNA into spike protein, which the immune system learns to recognize. The mRNA degrades quickly, leaving only immune memory to fight future infection.
